title: the Shiva Purana (selections)
hook: Daksha holds a great sacrifice and leaves out one guest, his own son-in-law Shiva, and his daughter Sati decides to go anyway

segments.voice: Yesterday the Shiva Purana opened with a pillar of fire, and the god who came back honest: I couldn't find the end. Where did you say I don't know? Day one thousand one hundred nineteen.
screen: `I COULDN'T FIND THE END.` · `A SECOND SELECTION.`

segments.voice: From the slopes of Kailash, Sati sees them go by in the sky: gods and their wives, dressed for a celebration, all heading the same way. She asks where they're going. To her father's house. Daksha, her father, is holding a great sacrifice, a yajna, and the guests are streaming in. Everyone, it seems, except Sati and her husband. Daksha has left out his own son-in-law. He's left out Shiva. Sati turns to her husband and says she wants to go. That's today's selection from the Shiva Purana: a family quarrel that shakes the world.
screen: `GUESTS IN THE SKY.` → `EVERYONE BUT SHIVA.` → `SATI WANTS TO GO.`

segments.voice: The grudge is old. In the Shiva Purana, at an earlier gathering of the gods, Daksha walked in and the others rose to honor him, but Shiva stayed seated. Daksha took it as an insult and never let it go. To him, Shiva was an embarrassment of a son-in-law: smeared with ash, wandering cremation grounds, no fine house. Now Sati wants to go to her father's sacrifice. Shiva tells her plainly that it's a bad idea. To go where you haven't been invited, he says, brings dishonor, and her father means to insult them. But it's her father's house. She can't believe her own family will turn her away. So she goes. And it's worse than Shiva said. At the sacrifice there's no portion set aside for Shiva at all. Her father greets her coldly and speaks of her husband with contempt in front of everyone. Sati won't hear it. She rebukes her father in front of the gods, and then she gives up her body there and then, by the power of her own yoga, rather than live as the daughter of the man who mocked Shiva. When word reaches Shiva, his grief becomes fury. From his matted hair he brings out Virabhadra, a terrible warrior, who storms the sacrifice and wrecks it. Daksha is killed. And here the story turns once more. When the gods beg, Shiva relents. Daksha is brought back to life, but with the head of a goat. A proud man, given a humbler face and a second chance. The story holds a lot of feeling: a daughter's loyalty, a husband's grief, a father's pride. And it treats contempt as no small thing: mocking someone in front of the people who love them is enough, here, to bring down a great sacrifice.
screen: `AN OLD GRUDGE AT A GATHERING.` · `SATI GOES ANYWAY.` · `SHE WILL NOT HEAR HIM MOCKED.` · `A GOAT'S HEAD AND A SECOND CHANCE.` · then, large: `A FAMILY QUARREL SHAKES THE WORLD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: sit with an old grudge, gently. Settle, and let the breath slow. Let one come up: a slight you've carried, a time someone didn't stand up for you, or you didn't stand up for them. Don't relive the whole scene. Just notice how long you've been carrying it, the way Daksha carried his. Where does it sit in the body? On each out-breath, loosen your grip on it by one finger. You don't have to let it go today. If you pray, you can bring it to Shiva, or to God, in your own words. The bell holds the time.
The Shiva Purana. Today's selection: Daksha's sacrifice, where Sati would not hear her husband mocked, and a proud father got a goat's head and a second chance.
Your line: the Shiva Purana, in selections. Today, if someone you care about is talked down in front of you, say one kind true word for them. Day one thousand one hundred nineteen.

howItsDone: Hindus tell the story of Sati and Daksha's sacrifice in the Shiva Purana and other Puranas; Shaiva temples honor Virabhadra, and Sati's story is linked to the shakti pithas, places sacred to the goddess.

fork.setup: you're Sati. your father is holding a great sacrifice and has invited the gods but not your husband. your husband says don't go. what do you do?

fork.reveal: Sati goes, sure her family won't turn her away. it's worse than Shiva said, and she will not hear him mocked.

notes: Selection two of this writer's four (Rudra Samhita, Sati Khanda). Paraphrased: Shiva not rising for Daksha at an earlier gathering; Daksha's contempt (ash, cremation grounds); Sati seeing the gods travel to the sacrifice; Shiva advising against going uninvited; no share set for Shiva; Sati's rebuke and yogic self-immolation; Virabhadra from Shiva's matted hair; Daksha killed and restored with a goat's head when the gods plead.
